name: Wav2Letter++
baseline: ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq (other end-to-end ASR training frameworks; the paper compares training time per batch against these)
workload: Training time per batch (4 utterances per GPU) of a 30M-parameter recurrent acoustic model and a 100M-parameter purely convolutional acoustic model (18 temporal convolution layers plus one linear layer), scaled from one GPU up to 64 GPUs, against ESPnet, Kaldi and OpenSeq2Seq.
claimed_speedup: In some cases more than 2x faster than other optimized frameworks for training end-to-end speech recognition networks; for the 30M-parameter model more than 15% faster than the next-best system even on a single GPU; training time scales linearly to 64 GPUs (the highest tested) for 100M-parameter models. Wording from the paper abstract and search-result summaries of the paper; the per-framework milliseconds-per-batch table was not seen.
hardware: Machines with eight NVIDIA Tesla V100 Tensor Core GPUs (SXM2 modules, 16 GB each), per search-result summary of the paper; CPU model not seen.
tradeoffs: Training toolkit for speech-recognition research, not a drop-in library replacement: it needs the ArrayFire tensor library and Flashlight (v0.2/0.3 branches), and the README says results reproduction needs Flashlight <= 0.3.2. Development moved into the Flashlight ASR application, so this repo is a frozen recipe and model collection. The category video-audio is the closest fit in this wave; the project is a machine-learning training system. The baselines are Python/TensorFlow/PyTorch/Kaldi systems, not C++ standard-library facilities.
caveats: Snippet only for the numbers: the repository README, v0.2 README and wiki contain no benchmark numbers and only link the paper (arXiv 1812.07625, ICASSP 2019 'wav2letter++: A Fast Open-source Speech Recognition System', doi 10.1109/ICASSP.2019.8683535). arxiv.org, ar5iv, sigport, deepai, hgpu, paperswithcode, academia.edu, huggingface and semantic scholar were all EGRESS_BLOCKED in this session, so the paper itself was not opened; the figures above come from WebSearch result summaries of the abstract and experiment setup. Tier is capped at C for that reason; a peer-reviewed ICASSP paper whose tables were read could be retiered to B (code is public but compiler flags, framework versions and CPU model are likely not all stated, so A is unlikely). The paper benchmark dates from late 2018 and the competitors were older versions. Licence discrepancy: README says MIT, the LICENSE file is a BSD 3-clause text (checked via raw.githubusercontent.com), recorded as BSD-3-Clause; the awesome-cpp tag said BSD. Last commit 2026-08-28 is an automated lint-fix commit by a bot, real development stopped when the code was consolidated into flashlight/flashlight.
